requirements.title: Above the wide-screen breakpoint, the /graph page shall display a pane-count control positioned beside the Options & help hamburger, independent of the layout-mode toggle

vision.paraphrase: An independent pane-count control (1-pane / 2-pane) sits in the header beside the Options & help hamburger, orthogonal to the existing force-directed/swim-lane mode toggle.
The pane-count control is positioned beside the Options & help hamburger and is always visible above the wide-screen breakpoint, ensuring discoverable access to dual-pane mode.

conops.paraphrase: When a visitor is on /graph above the wide-screen breakpoint, a pane-count control is visible in the header, independent from the layout-mode toggle.

requirements.title: Activating the pane-count control shall switch the board from 1-pane to 2-pane mode, rendering both the swim-lane and force-directed layouts side by side at approximately half width each

vision.paraphrase: In 2-pane mode both layouts render simultaneously side by side at roughly half width each, letting visitors compare data presentation styles without losing context.

conops.paraphrase: When a visitor clicks the pane-count toggle, the board splits into two side-by-side panes, each at approximately half the board's width.

requirements.title: In 2-pane mode, the swim-lane layout shall always render as the left pane and the force-directed layout as the right pane, regardless of which mode was active before switching
requirements.amended: 2026-07-18 — see the Note block in the feature file for the change-control record; originally traced to ConOps S13 step 3's 'active mode becomes primary pane' language, now a fixed left/right assignment discovered via live wrapup-epic verification of epic CU634Yc

vision.paraphrase: In 2-pane mode both layouts render simultaneously side by side, letting visitors compare data presentation styles; the specific left/right assignment was refined post-implementation to a fixed, predictable order.

conops.paraphrase: When toggling to 2-pane mode, the board splits into swim-lane and force-directed panes side by side (original step 3 language about 'active mode becomes primary' superseded by the amendment above).

requirements.title: Clicking a node in one pane while in 2-pane mode shall focus that same node in the other pane and update the shared side panel with that node's detail

vision.paraphrase: Node selection is synced across both panes and the shared side panel, so a click in one pane immediately updates the other.

conops.paraphrase: When a visitor clicks a node in one pane, that same node becomes focused in the other pane with connector lines or highlighting activated, and the shared side panel displays its detail.

requirements.title: Clicking a different node in the other pane shall update focus in both panes and the side panel together

vision.paraphrase: Node selection is synced across both panes and the shared side panel, maintaining state consistency as the visitor explores via either pane.

conops.paraphrase: When a visitor clicks a different node in the other pane, focus updates in both panes and the shared side panel together, showing the newly selected node's detail.

requirements.title: Deactivating the pane-count control while in 2-pane mode shall return the board to 1-pane mode, showing whichever layout mode was last focused or interacted with

vision.paraphrase: The pane-count toggle is a persistent control; toggling from 2-pane back to 1-pane restores the mode that was last focused, preserving navigation intent.

conops.paraphrase: When a visitor deactivates the pane-count control, the board returns to 1-pane mode displaying whichever layout mode was last focused or interacted with.

requirements.title: Below the wide-screen breakpoint, the pane-count control shall be hidden and the board shall render in 1-pane mode only

vision.paraphrase: Available only above a wide-screen breakpoint — below it, the control is hidden and the page behaves exactly as it does today (1-pane only), consistent with the existing 390px responsive-floor precedent.

conops.paraphrase: When a visitor opens /graph at 390px viewport width, the board lays out single-column with no dual-pane option visible, matching the existing responsive floor.
When a visitor is viewing /graph below the wide-screen breakpoint, the pane-count control is not visible and the board renders in 1-pane mode only.

requirements.title: If a visitor resizes the browser below the wide-screen breakpoint while in 2-pane mode, the board shall automatically fall back to 1-pane mode

vision.paraphrase: Below the wide-screen breakpoint, the page behaves exactly as it does today (1-pane only), consistent with the existing 390px responsive-floor precedent, automatically collapsing 2-pane mode if already active.

conops.paraphrase: When a visitor resizes the viewport below the wide-screen breakpoint while in 2-pane mode, the board automatically falls back to 1-pane mode and the pane-count control becomes hidden.
The Operational Constraints (§8) specify that 2-pane mode requires a wide-screen viewport; below it, the control is hidden and the board is 1-pane only.

requirements.title: Switching between 1-pane and 2-pane mode shall not trigger a new network request for graph-data.json or vector-index.json

vision.paraphrase: Both force-directed and swim-lane modes share the same node coloring, status dots, hover tooltips, and side-panel/search integration; switching is instant with no data refetch.

conops.paraphrase: When a visitor toggles between 1-pane and 2-pane mode, both panes reuse the already-fetched graph-data.json and vector-index.json with no new network requests.
